📋 Protocol Context

From protocol profile: f(x) Protocol v2 (AladdinDAO) / fxSAVE (ERC-4626 savings vault over the f(x) Stability Pool (fxSP), staked in a gauge through a Convex vault)

Architecture— how the asset works
What fxSAVE is: fxSAVE 0x7743e50F534a7f9F1791DdE7dCD89F7783Eefc39 (SavingFxUSD) is an ERC-4626 savings vault of f(x) Protocol v2. Its asset is fxSP 0x65C9A641afCEB9C0E6034e558A319488FA0FA3be, the share token of the f(x) Stability Pool, which holds fxUSD and USDC. A holder deposits fxSP and receives fxSAVE shares; fxSAVE stakes the fxSP and adds the rewards it earns, so one share is worth a growing amount of fxSP: 1.11 to 1.12 fxSP from 1 October to 15 November 2026. Morpho Blue 0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb, a lending market outside f(x), held about 47 percent of the fxSAVE supply as collateral on 15 November 2026 (30 to 48 percent in daily readings since 1 October).
The Stability Pool: fxUSD is f(x)'s stablecoin, minted as debt in its lending pools. fxSP (FxUSDBasePool) takes deposits of fxUSD, counted at 1.00, and of USDC, counted at the Chainlink USDC/USD price, and mints pool shares pro rata; deposits stop while USDC reads below 0.995. The pool is the liquidator of f(x)'s lending pools: a rebalance or liquidate call spends the pool's fxUSD, and its USDC when the fxUSD runs short, to repay a borrower's debt, and the caller pays the pool back at par and takes the collateral. fxSP keeps its USDC on hand or in an Aave V3 strategy 0xd023Aac0e2D46c93d4c6e8e2A449bF2d4687804f, from which a redeem pulls it back while Aave has unborrowed USDC. The strategy held less than 20 USDC from 1 October to 14 November 2026; on 14 and 15 November Safe 0x26B2 moved 31 million USDC into it, about 55 percent of the pool's assets. USDC, the strategy included, was 0 to 20 percent of the pool's assets in October 2026 and 2 to 80 percent from 1 to 15 November 2026; the rest was fxUSD.
Where the fxSP sits: fxSAVE's fxSP is staked in the fxSP gauge 0xEd92dDe3214c24Ae04F5f96927E3bE8f8DbC3289, f(x)'s staking contract for fxSP, except idle deposits below a threshold of 100 fxSP. fxSAVE deposits into the gauge directly and the stake is credited to a vault 0x4bFc5292DA18e32ED2354350e07e417cE4796f9C that Convex, an outside protocol that pools veFXN (locked FXN, f(x)'s governance token), created for fxSAVE and that fxSAVE owns: a minimal proxy clone, pool 36 in Convex's registry. Withdrawals go through that vault. fxSAVE held 90 to 98 percent of all fxSP from 1 October to 15 November 2026, 97 percent at the median, while its share supply fell from about 76 million in mid October to about 49 million on 15 November 2026.
Getting in: deposit and mint take fxSP; depositGauge takes fxSP that is already staked in the gauge. The f(x) router 0x33636D49FbefBE798e15e7F356E8DBef543CC708 offers routes that start from fxUSD or USDC in one transaction.
Leaving at once: redeem and withdraw burn the shares, withdraw the fxSP from the gauge through the Convex vault and pay fxSP to the receiver in the same transaction. From there fxSP pays out fxUSD and USDC pro rata: instantRedeem pays at once less a 1 percent fee that stays in the pool, and requestRedeem followed by redeem pays in full after a 1 hour cooldown. Holders of fxSP's fee waiver role (NO_INSTANT_REDEEM_FEE_ROLE) redeem at once with no fee.
Leaving through a request: requestRedeem on fxSAVE burns the shares, moves the fxSP into a holding contract of the owner's own (a LockedFxSaveProxy, created on first use) and files the fxSP redeem request from it. After the cooldown, claim pays the fxUSD and USDC to a receiver the owner names. claimFor does the same for a named owner; the router, which holds CLAIM_FOR_ROLE, calls it for users who exit through it.
Share price and nav: convertToAssets divides the fxSP that fxSAVE holds, idle and staked, by the share supply. fxSP counts its own assets with fxUSD at 1.00 and USDC at the Chainlink price. nav(), the USD value per share, instead prices the fxUSD with FxUSDPriceOracle 0x3eC677Ba393f2257ED0E1d37aA8442EB7F0953Fa: the exponential moving average (EMA) price of the Curve fxUSD/USDC pool 0x5018BE882DccE5E3F2f3B0913AE2096B9b3fB61f times Chainlink USDC/USD. fxSAVE.nav() multiplies fxSP's nav() by the fxSP per share.
Rewards: harvest() is open to anyone. It claims the gauge's reward tokens, wstETH and FXN, which the gauge pays straight to fxSAVE, pays the caller a 0.01 percent bounty and sends the rest to RewardHarvester 0x0559a1b22409Eef7559a5c88cbaA4e285e7b9C30. A keeper swaps it into fxUSD or USDC and hands it back to fxSAVE, which deposits it into fxSP and stakes it. Convex's 17 percent share applies only to FXN minted as gauge emissions; the fxSP gauge has had no emission weight since November 2025, so none is taken. The treasury's share of rewards is set to 0.
Peg keeping: PegKeeper 0x50562fe7e870420F5AAe480B7F94EB4ace2fcd70 exchanges fxSP's USDC for fxUSD, or the reverse, through a swap route, and must return at least par, with fxUSD counted at 1.00 and USDC at the Chainlink price. Any surplus goes to whoever called PegKeeper: the keeper's own account on a direct call, ProtocolTreasury 0x87d5e4cAaF4358A4337C10859c7107c7AEF4f8Ce on a relayed one. From January 2025 to 13 November 2026 it ran 830 times: 618.1 million USDC into fxUSD and 295.5 million fxUSD into USDC.
The gauge checkpoint: Every deposit into, withdrawal from and transfer of gauge shares runs a checkpoint. It first updates the accounting of each reward token, active and retired, then reads the gauge's weight from the GaugeController 0xe60eB8098B34eD775ac44B1ddE864e098C6d7f37 (admin: GaugeControllerOwner 0x1Ca7b82c4265835C7841cf29407217D820a7DADb). After the balance changes, the gauge reads veFXN's total supply and, through the boost proxy 0x1145f304d74f3295Fa38b82e7BB8704B0E187FA1, the veFXN boost of the account whose veFXN counts for the staker (its vote owner), which for fxSAVE's vault is Convex's voter proxy 0xd11a4Ee017cA0BECA8FA45fF2abFe9C6267b7881. The Convex vault reads the state of Convex MultiRewards 0x4187DC4998bB9f47389cD885A80a52A74EC8803c on every withdrawal and calls into it once Convex switches that contract's rewards on; they are off.
Governance: fxSAVE, fxSP, the gauge, PegKeeper and ProtocolTreasury are Transparent proxies under ProxyAdmin 0x9B54B7703551D9d0ced177A78367560a8B2eDDA4, owned by TimelockController 0x68863fb8855b04509a835082478D6E3D0bE4E61a with a 3 day delay; Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9) is its only proposer and canceller, and anyone can execute. The Timelock holds the admin role of fxSP, the gauge and PegKeeper and one of fxSAVE's two admin seats; Safe 0xA0FB1b11ccA5871fb0225B64308e249B97804E99 (6 of 9, the same nine owners) holds the other. Safe 0x26B2 directly owns the router, the boost proxy and the GaugeControllerOwner and manages the gauge's reward list. Safe 0x26B2 and Safe 0x28c921adAC4c1072658eB01a28DA06b5F651eF62 (3 of 4, four of the nine) hold ProtocolTreasury's admin role and can move fxSP's USDC into its strategy. Convex MultiRewards answers to Convex's reward manager, not to f(x). Keeper roles are held by externally owned accounts, one key each.
Scope: This report scans 20 contracts: fxSAVE, fxSP, the gauge, the Convex vault and reward contract, the keepers' contracts, the router, the governance contracts and the Curve pool. fxUSD, PoolManager and the lending pools are covered by the fxUSD report. OpenZeppelin audited SavingFxUSD, FxUSDBasePool and PegKeeper at commit 56a47ea (27 March to 5 May 2025); fxSP's implementation has been replaced since. SECBIT audited fxSAVE and the Stability Pool's USDC strategy (report of 17 March 2025).

📖 Terms— recurring protocol jargon
fxSP The share token of the f(x) Stability Pool (FxUSDBasePool). The pool holds fxUSD and USDC, and fxSP is what an fxSAVE share is a claim on.
Gauge The f(x) staking contract for fxSP. Staked fxSP earns the gauge's reward tokens, wstETH and FXN, as they are funded. fxSAVE keeps its fxSP there, in the name of its Convex vault.
Checkpoint The gauge's reward accounting step. It runs on every deposit, withdrawal and transfer of gauge shares, so every fxSAVE withdrawal passes through it.
Boost and veFXN FXN is f(x)'s governance token and veFXN is locked FXN. The gauge weights a staker's share of FXN emissions by the veFXN balance behind it (its boost), read through the boost proxy on every checkpoint. The fxSP gauge has no emission weight today, so the boost earns nothing, but the read still runs. fxSAVE's vault uses Convex's veFXN.
Convex vault A small contract Convex created for fxSAVE and that fxSAVE owns. fxSAVE's gauge stake is held in its name, so that the stake counts Convex's veFXN as its boost.
Par swap An exchange of fxUSD for USDC, or the reverse, inside fxSP at par value (fxUSD at 1.00 and USDC at the Chainlink price, so close to one for one), whatever fxUSD trades at in the market.
Surplus over par What a peg keeper's market route returns above the par value fxSP requires. fxSP pays it to PegKeeper's caller: the keeper on a direct call, ProtocolTreasury on a relayed one.
Cooldown The wait fxSP imposes between a redeem request and the fee free redeem: 1 hour, capped at 7 days in code.
Redeem request The exit route that starts with requestRedeem. On fxSAVE it moves the holder's fxSP into a holding contract, where it stays until it is claimed; once the cooldown has ended, claim pays fxUSD and USDC.
Fee waiver A role on fxSP (NO_INSTANT_REDEEM_FEE_ROLE) whose holder can redeem at once without the 1 percent instant fee.
Lever A privileged setting or function that this report tracks and grades by what it can do to the asset and how fast its holder can act.
🌐 Off-Chain Dependencies— risk that extends beyond the chain

5 control surface(s) extend beyond on-chain observability. Each entry shows what the analyst CAN observe (on-chain signal) alongside the off-chain dependencies it relies on.

1backing 🟠 HIGHfxSP holds fxUSD, counted at 1.00, next to USDC, and it is the only live liquidator of fxUSD's lending pools: a liquidation burns fxSP's fxUSD and the caller pays the pool back at par. fxSP has approved PoolManager for all of its USDC and fxUSD and books the amounts PoolManager reports. fxUSD's backing, its mint authority, PoolManager's own roles and the pools' oracles are outside this scan and are covered by the fxUSD report.
On-chain signal
fxSP totalYieldToken() and its USDC balance; PegKeeper getFxUSDPrice() (the Curve fxUSD/USDC EMA); fxUSD totalSupply().
Off-chain dependency
The f(x) v2 core: fxUSD 0x085780639CC2cACd35E474e71f4d000e2405d8f6, PoolManager 0x250893CA4Ba5d05626C785e8da758026928FCD24 and its pools.
Recovery path
None at this layer. A loss in fxUSD's backing reaches fxSAVE through the fxUSD that fxSP holds: 20 to 100 percent of fxSP's assets from 1 October to 15 November 2026. fxUSD's own supply fell from about 86 million on 4 November to about 20 million on 15 November 2026 while its price held at 1.00; almost all of the fall was debt repaid in the WBTC long pool (80.8 million on 16 October, 15.1 million on 15 November), which carries about three quarters of fxUSD's debt.
2governance 🔴 CRITICALfxSAVE's stake sits in its Convex vault, and every vault withdrawal calls Convex MultiRewards 0x4187DC4998bB9f47389cD885A80a52A74EC8803c once its rewards are switched on. Convex's reward manager can switch them on at any time, with no way back, and add reward tokens without a cap; each fxSAVE exit then loops over every one.
On-chain signal
MultiRewards rewardState() (1 = NoRewards, 2 = Active) and rewardTokenLength(), its Activate and RewardAdded events; Booster.rewardManager(); ConvexCore operators; the boost contract's delegated point for Convex's FxnVoterProxy (zero). Rewards were off and the reward list empty at block 26,408,442.
Off-chain dependency
Convex Finance: reward manager EOA 0xe7Ac460137CCD6173DB6992529013D672d4F0087 (set by the Booster's owner ConvexCore 0xCC07e8BA6bc8aeb18C4AE110C3Da9c7Dce4A3e74, whose operators are Safe 0xa3C5A1e09150B75ff251c1a7815A07182c3de2FB (3 of 5), which can make any call, and FxGaugeExecutor 0xD2c4c902D3F6882Dd9E8C18218CBD788c7CD4835, which can only cast Convex's gauge votes). fxSAVE's vault also shares the veFXN boost of Convex's FxnVoterProxy 0xd11a4Ee017cA0BECA8FA45fF2abFe9C6267b7881, so the gauge reads that proxy's boost balance in every checkpoint; only Convex can delegate that boost away.
Recovery path
Nothing on Convex's side undoes activation or removes a reward token. f(x) can upgrade the gauge through the 3 day Timelock to release the vault's stake to fxSAVE; that Timelock's only proposer is Safe 0x26B2.
3governance 🟠 HIGHfxSP keeps its USDC on hand or in an Aave V3 strategy (AaveV3CompoundStrategy 0xd023Aac0e2D46c93d4c6e8e2A449bF2d4687804f). Every fxSP deposit, redeem and nav() reads the strategy's balance, so an Aave aToken that reverts stops fxSP's flows until an fxSP upgrade; USDC pushed into the strategy comes back only out of the unborrowed USDC in Aave's reserve. Since 15 November 2026 about 55 percent of fxSP's assets sit in the strategy.
On-chain signal
fxSP allocations(USDC), the strategy's totalSupply() and USDC transfers from fxSP to the strategy. alloc, kill and manage emit no event. The strategy held 31.00M USDC at block 26,422,000 (under 20 USDC from 1 October to 14 November 2026). Aave's USDC reserve (aEthUSDC 0x98C23E9d8f34FEFb1B7BD6a91B7FF122F4e16F5c) held 161.0M unborrowed USDC against 2,790.7M supplied on 15 November 2026, about 94 percent borrowed: USDC balanceOf(aEthUSDC) and aEthUSDC totalSupply(). In hourly readings from 16 October to 15 November 2026 the unborrowed USDC ranged from 0.2M (30 October) to 776M, median 147M, and was below fxSP's present 31M position in 15 of 720 readings, on six days between 16 and 30 October.
Off-chain dependency
Aave governance, which controls the Aave V3 Pool and aToken implementations.
Recovery path
An fxSP upgrade or an alloc change through the 3 day Timelock. With USDC in the strategy, a redeem that needs more USDC than fxSP has on hand also needs that much unborrowed USDC in Aave's reserve.
4compliance 🟠 HIGHfxSP's redeem and instantRedeem pay the fxUSD and the USDC leg in one call. If Circle blacklists fxSP or pauses USDC, every fxSP redeem reverts, both legs, and fxSP's USDC is frozen; fxSAVE's own redeem still pays fxSP shares.
On-chain signal
USDC isBlacklisted(fxSP) and paused() (both false at block 26,402,662); fxSP's USDC, on hand and in the Aave strategy: 0 to 20 percent of its assets in October 2026, 2 to 80 percent from 1 to 15 November 2026.
Off-chain dependency
Circle (USDC issuer).
Recovery path
An fxSP upgrade through the 3 day Timelock to settle without the USDC leg; otherwise none.
5oracle 🟢 LOWfxSP reads the USDC price (Chainlink USDC/USD) and, for nav(), the fxUSD price (the Curve fxUSD/USDC EMA) from FxUSDPriceOracle 0x3eC677Ba393f2257ED0E1d37aA8442EB7F0953Fa. fxSP's pointer to it is immutable, but the oracle is itself an upgradeable proxy under the same ProxyAdmin, and its admin (the Timelock) can re-point the Curve pool behind the fxUSD price. A USDC reading below 0.995 stops fxSP deposits; a reverting read stops deposits, liquidations and stabilize calls. Redeems do not read a price.
On-chain signal
fxSP getStableTokenPrice() against stableDepegPrice(); fxSP nav().
Off-chain dependency
Chainlink (USDC/USD feed) and the Curve fxUSD/USDC pool 0x5018BE882DccE5E3F2f3B0913AE2096B9b3fB61f.
Recovery path
An upgrade of the oracle or of fxSP through the 3 day Timelock. fxSAVE's exits do not depend on it. The oracle's own upgrade path is graded in the upgrades lever.

🔮 Exit, Backing and Pricing Tripwires— live settings and balances that decide whether fxSAVE's exit works, what backs a share, and how it is priced

Live-read each scan; a repointed feed or retuned delay is flagged in Changes-Since. Any change to a row shows in Changes Since Last Scan, except rows 9, 10, 14 to 16, 23 and 24, which move with the market and are shown for reference. Rows 1 to 4 are what the gauge reads on every fxSAVE withdrawal: the boost source, the gauge's weight in the GaugeController and the lengths of the two reward lists; Safe 0x26B2 sets all of them with no delay, and row 2 failing to read is itself the signal. Row 5 is the gauge's liquidity manager, which would take custody of all staked fxSP once set. Rows 6 to 8 are Convex's side of the exit path. Rows 9 to 13 are what backs fxSP and where its USDC sits; rows 9 and 10 give the mix that the par swap levers can reach. Row 11 is the USDC a Safe has pushed into Aave: it stays in Changes Since so that a push shows there, and it also creeps up with Aave interest on every scan while the strategy is funded. Rows 14 to 16 are the prices and the share value. Rows 17 and 18 are fxSP's exit terms; row 19 is the USDC price below which fxSP stops deposits. Rows 20 and 21 are Circle's switches over the USDC leg. Row 22 is the delay in front of every upgrade through the ProxyAdmin; changes to the router Diamond's code have none. Rows 23 and 24 are Aave's USDC reserve: fxSP can withdraw row 11 only out of row 23, the USDC nobody has borrowed. Row 25 is the strategy slot for fxSP's fxUSD, empty at every reading since March 2025: Aave V3's USDC reserve is the only lending venue the pool has used, through this strategy and the one before it.

🎚️ Critical Parameter Levers— the one-tx risk levers to watch

14 on-chain parameter levers curated as high-impact for lender-side risk. Each is a singular setter / function call that flips the asset's risk surface — direct dilution, safety-mechanism closure, authority transfer, or oracle repointing.

1Boost source of the gauge checkpoint: updateVeBoost(address), and the transfer of the proxy's ownership 🔴 CRITICALon VotingEscrowProxy (0x1145f304d74f3295Fa38b82e7BB8704B0E187FA1)
Role gate
owner(): Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9), no delay. Ownable2Step; both steps are instant.
Live current value (as of block 19,287,263)
0x8Cc02c0D9592976635E98e6446ef4976567E7A81
1 recorded change(s); last setter 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
Threshold
veBoost() != 0x8Cc02c0D9592976635E98e6446ef4976567E7A81 (any UpdateVeBoost event); owner() != Safe 0x26B2 or pendingOwner() != 0x0 (OwnershipTransferStarted, OwnershipTransferred). Triage: simulate an fxSAVE redeem.
Impact
The gauge asks this proxy for an account's boosted veFXN balance on every deposit, withdrawal and transfer. The owner can point it at any contract that answers one balance call. If that contract then reverts, every fxSAVE redeem, withdraw and requestRedeem reverts. No principal moves, and requests already filed can still be claimed, but new exits stay closed until the gauge is upgraded, which takes 3 days and must be proposed by the same Safe.
2Gauge weights with no upper bound: changeGaugeWeight(address,uint256), changeTypeWeight(int128,uint256), and the hand over of the GaugeController's admin 🔴 CRITICALon GaugeControllerOwner (0x1Ca7b82c4265835C7841cf29407217D820a7DADb)
Role gate
DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9), no delay. This contract is the admin of GaugeController 0xe60eB8098B34eD775ac44B1ddE864e098C6d7f37 and can hand that seat to any address in two calls.
Threshold
Any NewGaugeWeight or NewTypeWeight event on the GaugeController for the fxSP gauge 0xEd92dDe3214c24Ae04F5f96927E3bE8f8DbC3289 or its type that a normalizeGaugeWeight call did not produce; gauge_relative_weight(fxSP gauge) reverting; GaugeController admin() != GaugeControllerOwner (CommitOwnership, ApplyOwnership); RoleGranted on GaugeControllerOwner.
Impact
The gauge reads its relative weight from the GaugeController for every week since its last checkpoint. These setters accept any number, and a weight large enough to overflow that calculation makes the read revert from the next weekly boundary. From then on every fxSAVE exit reverts, and a later weight change does not repair the week already started. The repair is a gauge upgrade: 3 days, proposed by the same Safe.
3Gauge reward list with no cap: registerRewardToken(address,address) 🔴 CRITICALon fxSP gauge, SharedLiquidityGauge (0xEd92dDe3214c24Ae04F5f96927E3bE8f8DbC3289)
Role gate
REWARD_MANAGER_ROLE: Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9), no delay. The role admin is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, held by the Timelock only, so a new holder needs a 3 day operation and then acts at once.
Threshold
getActiveRewardTokens() != [FXN 0x365AccFCa291e7D3914637ABf1F7635dB165Bb09, wstETH 0x7f39C581F595B53c5cb19bD0b3f8dA6c935E2Ca0] or getHistoricalRewardTokens() not empty; any RegisterRewardToken event; REWARD_MANAGER_ROLE holder set != {Safe 0x26B2}.
Impact
Every checkpoint, so every fxSAVE exit, loops over the gauge's active reward tokens and then over its retired ones. The manager can add tokens without limit, and removing one only moves it to the retired list, so the loop can only grow. Long enough, it needs more gas than a transaction may use and every exit reverts. The manager's own role cannot shorten the list; the repair is a gauge upgrade through the Timelock.
4Par swap of fxSP's USDC and fxUSD by the keeper: stabilize(address,uint256,bytes) 🟠 HIGHon PegKeeper (0x50562fe7e870420F5AAe480B7F94EB4ace2fcd70)
Role gate
STABILIZE_ROLE: EOA 0x4215F2014239Cf0E1A8617b31Fcaf88AaC6e4779 and ProtocolTreasury 0x87d5e4cAaF4358A4337C10859c7107c7AEF4f8Ce (a relay, see its own entry), no delay. The role admin is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, held by the Timelock only.

Threshold
Arbitrage events on fxSP 0x65C9A641afCEB9C0E6034e558A319488FA0FA3be: USDC leaving while PegKeeper getFxUSDPrice() is below 1e18, the size against fxSP's USDC balance, and bonusOut with its receiver; STABILIZE_ROLE holder set != {EOA 0x4215, ProtocolTreasury}.
Impact
The keeper swaps fxSP's USDC for fxUSD, or the reverse, through a route it chooses. fxSP checks only that it gets back at least par, with fxUSD counted at 1.00; it checks neither fxUSD's market price nor the size. While fxUSD trades below 1.00 the keeper can turn all of fxSP's USDC into fxUSD in one call, with no capital, and keep the surplus over par. fxSP's share count never falls, but its holders, of which fxSAVE is 90 to 98 percent, are left with discounted fxUSD in place of USDC: a loss of up to the discount times the USDC swapped.

Impact
The same swap as the PegKeeper entry, called through the treasury. The keeper still picks the route and the minimum; the surplus over par lands in the treasury, which its two admin Safes can withdraw. Either admin Safe, the smaller one 3 of 4, can hand this relay to any address at once. That bypasses the 3 day wait a STABILIZE grant takes on the PegKeeper itself.

NO_INSTANT_REDEEM_FEE_ROLE holder set != the seven above (RoleGranted, RoleRevoked on fxSP); InstantRedeem events by a holder in the same transaction as a Deposit of fxUSD while PegKeeper getFxUSDPrice() is below 1e18.
Impact
fxSP takes fxUSD deposits at a count of 1.00 with no check of fxUSD's price, and a redeem pays fxUSD and USDC pro rata. A holder of this role can deposit fxUSD and redeem at once with no fee, and repeat, which swaps fxUSD into fxSP's USDC at par in one transaction. While fxUSD trades below 1.00 that takes the discount on the USDC out of fxSP, as the keeper's swap does. Anyone can do the same, but only after the 1 hour cooldown or at the 1 percent instant fee, so in a shallow discount the role holders and the keepers are the only immediate takers.

The Timelock itself (TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE and the caller check of updateDelay), so each change is a queued operation that waits the current delay. PROPOSER_ROLE and CANCELLER_ROLE: Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9) only.
Threshold
getMinDelay() != 259200 (MinDelayChange); PROPOSER_ROLE or CANCELLER_ROLE holder set != {Safe 0x26B2}; TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE holder set != {Timelock}; any CallScheduled whose target is the Timelock.
Impact
The 3 day delay is the only notice in front of upgrades, strategy allocation and the gauge's custody setter. The delay has no minimum in code, and one Safe proposes and cancels everything, so there is no independent veto. A queued call that shortens the delay or adds a proposer is the earliest sign that this notice is about to weaken.
12Payout of another owner's matured redeem request: claimFor(address,address), and the grant of CLAIM_FOR_ROLE 🟠 HIGHon fxSAVE, SavingFxUSD (0x7743e50F534a7f9F1791DdE7dCD89F7783Eefc39)
Role gate
CLAIM_FOR_ROLE: router Diamond 0x33636D49FbefBE798e15e7F356E8DBef543CC708 (see its own entry). The role admin is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, held by the Timelock (3 days) and by Safe 0xA0FB1b11ccA5871fb0225B64308e249B97804E99 (6 of 9) with no delay, which can also remove the Timelock's seat.
Threshold
CLAIM_FOR_ROLE holder set != {router Diamond}; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder set != {Timelock, Safe 0xA0FB} (RoleGranted, RoleRevoked on fxSAVE); a Claim event whose fxSP payout goes to an address other than the owner or the router.
Impact
A redeem request moves the owner's fxSP into a holding contract until fxSP's cooldown ends. A holder of this role can then pay that fxSP to any address, and Safe 0xA0FB can give the role to any address at once. It reaches only requests already filed and matured; fxSAVE shares with no open request are out of reach, and the share price is untouched. For a FiRM market this is a design rule: exit with redeem, which pays fxSP at once, or claim a request as soon as its cooldown ends.
13Router facet changes: diamondCut((address,uint8,bytes4[])[],address,bytes), approveTarget(address,address), transferOwnership(address) 🟠 HIGHon router Diamond (0x33636D49FbefBE798e15e7F356E8DBef543CC708)
Role gate
owner(): Safe 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF (6 of 9), no delay. The owner transfer is a single step.
Threshold
Any DiamondCut event; facetAddresses() changing; a new approved call target; owner() != Safe 0x26B2 (OwnershipTransferred).
Impact
The router holds CLAIM_FOR_ROLE on fxSAVE and a fee waiver on fxSP, and users who exit through it have approved it to spend their fxSAVE. Its owner can replace its code at once, so new code could use both roles and those approvals for anyone it chooses. It cannot reach fxSAVE held with no approval to the router and no open redeem request.
14fxSP exit terms: updateRedeemCoolDownPeriod(uint256), updateInstantRedeemFeeRatio(uint256) 🟡 MEDIUMon fxSP, FxUSDBasePool (0x65C9A641afCEB9C0E6034e558A319488FA0FA3be)

DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE: Timelock 0x68863fb8855b04509a835082478D6E3D0bE4E61a (3 days; only proposer and canceller Safe 0x26B2, open executor).
Live current value (as of block 24,374,323)
10000000000000000 (0.010000e18)
5 recorded change(s); last setter 0x26B2ec4E02ebe2F54583af25b647b1D619e67BbF
Threshold
redeemCoolDownPeriod() != 3600 (UpdateRedeemCoolDownPeriod); instantRedeemFeeRatio() != 1e16 (UpdateInstantRedeemFeeRatio); any CallScheduled on the Timelock targeting fxSP with either setter.
Impact
The wait between a redeem request and the fee free redeem can be raised to 7 days, and the fee on an instant redeem to 5 percent; both limits are in code. Either makes leaving fxSP slower or dearer, which is the last step of an fxSAVE exit. Lowering either to zero would open the par swap of the fee waiver entry to everyone. Behind the Timelock, so a change is public for 3 days first.
